Section 2.1 · Orientation

Make programs choose.

Unit 1 made programs collect, store and calculate. Unit 2 adds selection, allowing the program to choose an appropriate route.

7 minread3examples

In this unit, you will move from asking one precise question to building complete programs with several tested routes.

Your route through Unit 2

01 · COMPARE

Test a value

Use operators such as ==, > and >= to produce True or False.

02 · SELECT

Choose a route

Use if, elif and else so only the appropriate instructions run.

03 · TEST

Prove it works

Trace every possible route and test values just below, on and just above each boundary.

The compare, decide, route model

01 · COMPARE

Ask a precise question

Use a comparison such as score >= 50.

02 · DECIDE

Produce a Boolean

The condition evaluates to either True or False.

03 · ROUTE

Run the correct branch

Indented instructions belong to the selected route.

CONTROL_SYSTEM.PY
temperature = 28

if temperature >= 25:
    print("Cooling system on")
else:
    print("Temperature normal")
Cooling system on

Selection sits inside a sequence

Python still reads the program from top to bottom. When it reaches a selection, it tests the condition, runs one appropriate route, then continues with the instructions after the selection. Think of the route as a controlled detour, not a restart.

✓

Keep the question precise

Before writing code, say the boundary in plain English. “16 or older” becomes age >= 16, not age > 16.

Section 2.2 · Workbook 07

Test values precisely.

Comparison operators ask exact questions. Their Boolean results become the conditions used by selection statements.

9 minread5examples

A comparison is an expression. Python evaluates it and returns True or False.

The six comparison operators

OperatorMeaningExampleResult
==Equal to7 == 7True
!=Not equal to7 != 5True
>Greater than7 > 7False
<Less than4 < 7True
>=Greater than or equal to7 >= 7True
<=Less than or equal to8 <= 7False
COMPARE.PY
age = 15
minimum_age = 15

print(age >= minimum_age)
print(age == minimum_age)
print(age < minimum_age)
True True False

Assignment is not equality

STORE

= assigns

score = 10 stores a value in a variable.

TEST

== compares

score == 10 asks whether two values match.

RESULT

A Boolean is returned

The comparison produces True or False.

Inclusive boundaries

Just below14 → False
On the boundary15 → True
Just above16 → True

Section 2.3 · Workbook 07
Run code conditionally.
A simple if statement runs an indented block only when its condition is True.
8 minread4examples

  

    
Use a simple if when an action is optional. If the condition is False, Python skips the indented block.

    
Anatomy of a simple if

    
SIMPLE_IF.PY
balance = 24

if balance < 25:       # condition and colon
    print("Low balance")  # indented branch

print("Check complete")  # always runs
Low balance
Check complete

    
Four structural rules
Start with if
Python recognises this keyword as the beginning of a selection.
Write a Boolean condition
The expression must evaluate to True or False.
Finish with a colon
The colon tells Python that an indented block follows.
Indent the owned instructions
Use four spaces consistently. Unindented code is outside the branch.

    
!
Indentation changes behaviour
Indentation is part of Python’s syntax. It shows which instructions belong to the condition.

    
QUICK CHECK 2.3
What happens when a simple if condition is False?

    
Simple selection complete
You can identify the condition, colon and indented branch.



  
Section 2.4 · Workbook 07
Choose one of two routes.
An if and else structure handles two mutually exclusive outcomes. Exactly one branch runs.
9 minread4examples

  

    
Use if and else when every valid input must follow one of two routes.

    
The two-route pattern

    
TWO_ROUTES.PY
order_total = 25

if order_total >= 25:
    print("Free delivery")
else:
    print("Delivery charge applies")
Free delivery

    
Else never has a condition
The else branch means “all remaining cases”. It has no comparison after it, but it still needs a colon and indentation.

    
2
One decision, two routes
The branches are mutually exclusive. Python cannot run both branches from the same if/else structure.

    
Two separate if statements are different
INDEPENDENT_CHECKS.PY
score = 84

if score >= 50:
    print("Pass")
if score >= 80:
    print("High score")
Pass
High score

    
QUICK CHECK 2.4
When should else be used?

    
Two routes understood
You can distinguish a paired if/else from independent checks.



  
Section 2.5 · Workbook 08
Build several routes.
Use elif to test further conditions. Python follows the first True route and skips the rest of the chain.
10 minread5examples

  

    
elif means “else if”. It allows one selection structure to choose from several ordered routes.

    
The multi-route pattern

    
ELIF_ROUTES.PY
score = 72

if score >= 80:
    band = "Distinction"
elif score >= 60:
    band = "Merit"
elif score >= 40:
    band = "Pass"
else:
    band = "Working towards"

print(band)
Merit

    
Order is part of the algorithm
>= 80Test the most demanding boundary first.
>= 60This route receives values not already caught above.
>= 40Continue from high boundaries to low boundaries.
elseFinish with every remaining value.

    
!
A correct condition can be in the wrong place
If score >= 40 appears first, a score of 90 matches it immediately. Python then skips the higher routes.

    
CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT
Trace the first True route
Change the score and see which condition captures it.

    
QUICK CHECK 2.5
Why are descending boundaries normally used in this example?

    
Decision routes complete
You can construct and order an if/elif/else chain.



  
Section 2.6 · Workbook 08
Combine conditions.
Logical operators join or reverse Boolean expressions, allowing a program to make decisions from several requirements.
11 minread6examples

  

    
Use and, or and not when one comparison is not enough to describe the rule.

    
Three logical operators
AND
Both must be True
age >= 14 and consent == "yes"
OR
At least one must be True
member == "yes" or code == "SAVE"
NOT
Reverse a Boolean
not account_locked

    
LOGIC.PY
age = 15
consent = "yes"

if age >= 14 and consent == "yes":
    print("Eligible")
else:
    print("Not eligible")
Eligible

    
Truth patterns
True and TrueTrue
True and FalseFalse
True or FalseTrue
False or FalseFalse

    
Keep compound conditions readable
Use parentheses when they make the intended grouping clearer. A readable condition is easier to test and less likely to hide a logic error.

    
CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT
AND or OR?
Change the values and operator to see how the final Boolean changes.

Section 2.7 · Workbook 09
Build complete decision systems.
Validation protects the program from impossible data. Nested selection handles decisions that only matter after another route succeeds.
12 minread6examples

  

    
A decision system is more than one condition. It validates inputs, controls dependent questions and produces a clear result.

    
Validate before processing

    
VALIDATION.PY
score = 104

if 0 <= score <= 100:
    print("Valid score")
else:
    print("Invalid score")
Invalid score

    
A decision inside a decision

    
NESTED.PY
registered = "yes"
overdue = "no"

if registered == "yes":
    if overdue == "no":
        print("Loan approved")
    else:
        print("Return overdue items first")
else:
    print("Registration required")
Loan approved

    
Nested or combined?
DEPENDENT
Use nesting
The second question only makes sense after the first succeeds.
ONE RULE
Use a logical operator
Both comparisons belong to one clear requirement.
CLARITY
Prefer readable code
Choose the structure that makes the algorithm easiest to trace.

    
↳
Line up each else carefully
Indentation shows which if an else belongs to. Read nested code vertically before tracing its values.

    
QUICK CHECK 2.7
Why validate a score before assigning a band?

    
Decision systems complete
You can combine validation and dependent decisions.



  
Section 2.8 · Revision
Trace every route.
Reliable selection depends on correct syntax, correct boundaries and systematic testing across every possible branch.
12 minread7examples

  

    
Do not test only a comfortable middle value. Good testing targets boundaries, invalid data and every route through the algorithm.

    
Three common selection faults
FaultWhat happensTypical repair
Syntax errorThe program cannot run.Add the missing colon or repair indentation.
Boundary errorAn exact edge value follows the wrong route.Check whether > should be >=.
Route-order errorA broad condition catches a value too early.Order overlapping routes from most specific to least specific.

    
Worked debugging example

    
FAULTY_ACCESS.PY
username = input("Username: ")
pin = input("PIN: ")

if username == "admin" or pin == "2468":
    print("Access granted")
else:
    print("Access denied")

    
Logic error: or grants access when either detail is correct. Authentication requires both details, so replace it with and.

    
Boundary test design
Just below49
On the boundary50
Just above51
For a pass boundary of 50, these three values expose whether the comparison includes the boundary correctly.

    
A disciplined repair cycle
Predict
Write the route and output you expect for a chosen test value.
Trace
Evaluate each condition in order and stop at the first True route.
Compare
Compare the predicted and actual outputs. Identify the exact point they differ.
Repair and retest
Change one cause, then repeat normal, boundary and invalid tests.

    
QUICK CHECK 2.8
Which values best test a pass boundary of 50?

Core knowledgeQuick reference & examplesBefore you runErrors & fixes


Core knowledge
The six foundations to know with confidence
1What is a condition?
A condition is a statement that evaluates to True or False. It controls whether a route is followed.
2Comparison operators
OperatorMeaning
==Equal to
!=Not equal to
> <Greater / less than
>= <=At least / at most
3If, elif and else
if tests the first condition. elif checks another route. else handles everything remaining.
4Boolean logic
Use and when both conditions must be true, or when either may be true, and not to reverse a result.
5Types of selection
Simple selection makes one decision. Multiple selection chooses between several routes. Nested selection places one decision inside another.
6Plan the route
Identify the question, possible outcomes and default route before coding. Use the simplest selection structure that solves the problem.


Quick reference & examples
Copy, adapt and test these reliable patterns
1Basic if statement

PYTHON PATTERN
if score >= 70:

else:

✓ Checklist: before you run
⚠ Common errors & how to fix them
ErrorWhat it meansHow to fix it
IndentationErrorA block is not aligned correctly.Indent all statements belonging to the same route.
SyntaxErrorPython cannot understand the selection.Check colons, brackets, quotes and spelling.
NameErrorA variable is used before assignment.Define the variable before the condition.
ValueErrorInput cannot be converted.Validate or handle the input before converting.
Logic errorThe program runs but takes the wrong route.Check operator choice and condition order.

Unit 2 glossary
AND
A logical operator that is True only when both conditions are True.
Boolean
A value that is either True or False.
Boundary
An edge value where the expected route changes.
Branch
A group of instructions controlled by a selection statement.
Comparison
An expression that compares values and returns a Boolean.
Condition
The Boolean expression that controls a decision.
Equality operator
The == operator used to test whether values match.
Else
The final route used when no earlier condition is True.
Elif
An additional condition tested after the opening if.
If
The keyword that begins a selection and tests its first condition.
Inclusive boundary
A boundary included using >= or <=.
Logical operator
An operator such as and, or or not.
Nesting
Placing one selection structure inside another.
NOT
A logical operator that reverses a Boolean result.
OR
A logical operator that is True when at least one condition is True.
Route order
The sequence in which conditions are tested.
Selection
An algorithm construct that chooses which instructions run.
Validation
Checking that input is sensible and acceptable before processing.
